notes:
I matched 61 of the 65 stations to a row in Findlay 1879. The other four have no entry: Fair Isle and Hynish Signal Tower (observer's stations, not lights), North Carr L.V. (no vessel listed in 1879) and Fidra (not in the 1879 edition). I could not find Ailsa Craig in the table either, so as far as I can tell that is five nulls, not four. No station needed extra_rows: every station Findlay gives as several lights (Pentland Skerries, Girdleness, Isle of May, Monach Isles, Pladda, Stornoway) is printed in a single row. The one row shared by two stations is p48r16 (Hoy Sound), which goes to both hoy-low and hoy-high.

Things to check:
1) The Hoy Sound row p48r16 has one position, 58 56.1 / 3 16.5, for both lights. You may need another source to get a separate position for each.
2) The Stornoway row p49r12 holds two lights: the Arnish Point tower and the reflected light on the beacon. Only part 1 is the station's own light.
3) Findlay's Montrose Harbour row (p47r10) should not be mixed up with MONTROSE NESS = Scurdie Ness (p47r9).
4) McArthur's Head (p50r10): the description says 'S. end of Islay', but the latitude fits the Sound of Islay site. Check the longitude against the scan.
5) Some year cells are damaged or empty: Lamlash/Holy Isle '[?]877', Little Ross '184[?]', and no year for Rhuvaal (Rudha Mhail). Check these on the scan.
6) There are misprints in the reports' printed names that I resolved by position or coast order: 'North Uist' (= North Unst), 'Bona' (= Rona), 'Conan Ferry' (= Corran Ferry), 'Rhinns of May' (= Rhinns of Islay). There is also 'Tarbat Head', which I took to mean Tarbat Ness.
7) The reports list the North Carr / Carr Rock lightship from 1885. Findlay 1879 has nothing for it, so its position must come from a later list.
8) Two places are called Sanda: Start Point's row puts it on Sanda (Sanday) Island in Orkney, and SANDA ISLAND (p50r15) is off Kintyre. They are matched to different stations.
